Below is the complete 12‑week Couch‑to‑5K plan tailored for your 24‑year‑old client with exercise‑induced asthma (EIA), integrating warm‑ups/cool‑downs, asthma precautions, 2 strength sessions/week, progressive intervals, one tempo session/week (from Week 7), Parkrun test in Week 8, and a race‑prep (taper) week in Week 12. Use RPE (rate of perceived exertion) where pace guidance is needed: Easy = RPE 3–4/10, Tempo = RPE 6–7/10, 5K/interval effort = RPE 7–8/10. Always get medical clearance, have the SABA inhaler available, and follow the safety rules below.

Safety & asthma rules (must read)
- Warm up thoroughly (12–15+ min) before every run; extend to 15 min before interval/tempo/race sessions. Warm‑up: brisk walk → easy jog → dynamic drills → 4–6 strides (20–30 s).
- Take SABA 10–15 min before sessions if that is his GP routine; carry inhaler during workouts.
- In cold weather, use a buff/scarf, extend the walking portion of warm‑up, or move sessions indoors.
- If coughing/wheezing/chest tightness occurs: stop, use inhaler, rest. If symptoms don’t improve or inhaler use increases, consult GP and reduce intensity.
- Progress hard work slowly. When in doubt, repeat a week rather than push on.

Weekly structure (typical)
- 3 run sessions/week (Mon/Wed/Fri or Mon/Wed/Sat) — mix of easy runs, intervals, tempo (from Week 7), long/easy.
- 2 strength sessions/week (Tue & Thu) — Strength 1 = heavier/longer (30–35 min), Strength 2 = lighter/maintenance & mobility (20–25 min).
- Sat or Sun: rest/active recovery or Parkrun in Week 8.
- Keep runs on non‑consecutive days where possible. Ensure one easy day after any interval/tempo session.

Warm‑up (every session)
- 5–8 min brisk walk → easy jog
- 2–4 min dynamic mobility/activation (leg swings, hip circles, walking lunges, ankle rolls)
- 2–4 min progressive easy jog → 4–6 strides (especially before intervals/tempos)
- Take SABA 10–15 min before warm‑up if that’s his routine

Cool‑down (every session)
- 5–10 min slow walk/jog
- Static stretching: calves, quads, hamstrings, glutes (1×30 s each)
- Breathing control (diaphragmatic breaths) if helpful

Strength sessions (two per week) — overview
- Strength 1 (Tue): 30–35 min — posterior chain, single‑leg strength, core. 3 sets of main lifts, 60–90 s rest.
- Strength 2 (Thu): 20–25 min — maintenance circuit, mobility, breathing drills. 2 rounds.
- Avoid heavy lower‑body lifts within 48–72 hours of the heaviest interval session; in Week 12 keep strength very light.

Progression notes for intervals & tempo
- Intervals introduced Week 5 and progress in duration and specificity through Weeks 11–12.
- Tempo runs start Week 7 and build to 20 min tempo by Week 10.
- Limit hard interval sessions to 1 per week until Week 9; add a second short session in Week 10 only if tolerated.
- Use RPE and symptom log to guide progression. Traffic‑light rule: Green (no extra inhaler, OK) → progress; Amber (extra single inhaler puff, brief symptoms) → hold/step back; Red (prolonged symptoms/more inhaler) → revert to base & GP review.

Full 12‑Week program (week-by-week). Each week lists 3 run sessions and 2 strength sessions. Warm‑up/cool‑down and asthma precautions apply to all sessions.

Weeks 1–2 — Establish routine, breathing control, long warm‑ups
Goal: get moving regularly, practice long warm‑ups and breathing, introduce light strength.

Week 1
- Mon — Run A (20–25 min): Warm‑up 12–15 min. 6×(1:00 easy jog + 2:00 brisk walk). Cool‑down.
- Tue — Strength 1 (30 min): Glute bridge 3×12; Bodyweight squat 3×12; Reverse lunges 3×8/leg; Plank 3×30 s; Single‑leg calf raise 3×12/leg.
- Wed — Run B (20 min): Warm‑up. 8×(1:00 jog + 1:30 walk). Cool‑down.
- Thu — Strength 2 (20 min): 2 rounds circuit: Step‑ups 12/leg; Side‑lying clamshell 12/side; Band row 12/arm; Dead bug 10/side.
- Fri — Run C (21 min): Warm‑up. 6×(1:30 jog + 2:00 walk). Cool‑down.
- Sat — Optional easy walk/mobility.
- Sun — Rest.

Week 2
- Mon — Run A: 1:00 jog + 2:00 walk ×6 (same as Wk1 A).
- Tue — Strength 1: same as Week 1; focus on form.
- Wed — Run B: 1:00 jog +1:30 walk ×8 (same).
- Thu — Strength 2: same circuit, 2 rounds.
- Fri — Run C: 1:30 jog + 2:00 walk ×6.
- Sat/Sun — Recovery/rest.

Weeks 3–4 — Increase interval lengths; begin light loaded strength
Goal: longer continuous intervals, introduce goblet/DB exercises.

Week 3
- Mon — Run A: Warm‑up. 7×(2:00 jog + 2:00 walk). Cool‑down.
- Tue — Strength 1: Single‑leg glute bridge 3×10/leg; Goblet squat 3×10; Bulgarian split squat 3×8/leg; Side plank 3×25–30 s; RDL (light DB) 3×8–10; Calf raises 3×15.
- Wed — Run B: Warm‑up. 6×(3:00 jog + 2:00 walk). Cool‑down.
- Thu — Strength 2: Circuit 2 rounds: Single‑leg RDL 10/leg; Push‑ups 10–12; Pallof press 10–12/side; Walking lunges 10/leg.
- Fri — Run C: Warm‑up. 3×(5:00 jog + 3:00 walk). Cool‑down.
- Sat/Sun — Recovery.

Week 4
- Mon — Run A: Warm‑up. 6×(4:00 jog + 2:00 walk) OR 7×(3:00 + 2:00) if preferred.
- Tue — Strength 1: Progress weight slightly on goblet/DB RDLs; 3 sets each.
- Wed — Run B: Warm‑up. 5×(5:00 jog + 3:00 walk).
- Thu — Strength 2: 2–3 rounds circuit (as Week 3).
- Fri — Run C: Warm‑up. 2×(8:00 jog + 3:00 walk) or 3×(5:00 +3:00).
- Sat/Sun — Active recovery/rest.

Weeks 5–6 — Move toward continuous running; introduce intervals
Goal: longer continuous blocks, first interval session introduced, increase strength load.

Week 5
- Mon — Run A: Warm‑up. 2×(8:00 easy jog + 3:00 walk). Cool‑down.
- Tue — Strength 1: DB RDL 3×8; Bulgarian split squat 3×8–10/leg; Step‑ups (weighted) 3×10/leg; Single‑leg glute bridge 3×10/leg; Plank w/arm reach 3×30–40 s; Calf raises 3×12–15.
- Wed — Run B (Interval intro): Warm‑up 15 min incl. 4 strides. 6×1:00 brisk runs (RPE ~7/10) with 2:00 easy jog/walk recovery. Cool‑down 8–10 min.
- Thu — Strength 2: 2–3 rounds: Kettlebell swings 12–15; TRX row 12; Lateral lunges 10/side; Bird‑dog 10/side.
- Fri — Run C: Warm‑up. Continuous 15 min easy jog + 5 min walk + 10 min easy jog (or 2×12 min with short walk). Cool‑down.
- Sat/Sun — Easy activity/rest.

Week 6
- Mon — Run A: Warm‑up. 20 min continuous easy run (if tolerated) or 2×10 min with 2 min walk.
- Tue — Strength 1: increase load on RDLs/step‑ups modestly.
- Wed — Run B (Intervals): Warm‑up 15 min. 8×1:00 brisk with 90–120 s recovery OR 5×90 s at slightly faster pace with 2:00 recovery. Cool‑down.
- Thu — Strength 2: lighter maintenance circuit + breathing drills.
- Fri — Run C: Warm‑up. 2×10–12 min easy jog with 2–3 min recovery between. Cool‑down.
- Sat/Sun — Rest/active recovery.

Weeks 7–8 — Build continuous time, introduce tempo, and Parkrun test in Week 8
Goal: 20–30 min continuous run capability; tempo introduction Week 7; Parkrun Week 8 (controlled test).

Week 7
- Mon — Run A: Warm‑up. 20 min continuous easy run. Cool‑down.
- Tue — Strength 1: heavier session — trap‑bar/DB RDL 3×5–8; Bulgarian split squat 3×8; Farmer carry 3×40–60 m; Hanging knee raise 3×10–12; calf work.
- Wed — Tempo (Intro): Warm‑up (15 min). 2×6 min tempo (RPE 6–7/10) with 3:00 easy jog between. Cool‑down.
- Thu — Strength 2: 2 rounds lighter circuit + mobility.
- Fri — Run C (Fartlek/light): Warm‑up. 20–25 min easy run with 6×30–45 s pickups (85% effort) with full recovery. Cool‑down.
- Sat — Easy walk or rest.
- Sun — Rest.

Week 8 — Parkrun test week (Parkrun on Sat)
- Monday — Run A: Easy 20–30 min. Strength 1 (move to Tue if preferred).
- Tuesday — Strength 1: moderate, reduce volume if feeling tired.
- Wednesday — Tempo: 10–12 min tempo OR 2×6 min tempo (shorter than usual) — keep intensity controlled.
- Thursday — Strength 2: light mobility and activation only.
- Friday — Easy 20–25 min + 4 strides in warm‑up; keep relaxed.
- Saturday — Parkrun (5K test). Race day plan:
  - 60–90 min pre: small carb snack; SABA 10–15 min before warm‑up if that’s his routine.
  - Warm‑up 15–20 min: walk → easy jog → mobility → 4–6 strides.
  - Race: conservative start; even/small negative split strategy. Carry inhaler.
  - Cool‑down 8–12 min + recovery snack.
- Sunday — Recovery: rest or easy active recovery. Monitor asthma; avoid heavy strength for 48 hours after Parkrun.

Weeks 9–10 — Build intensity and intervals; tempo to 20 min
Goal: consolidate endurance, add structured interval and tempo stimulus. May add second interval session in Week 10 if tolerated.

Week 9
- Mon — Run A: 25–30 min continuous easy run (conversational).
- Tue — Strength 1: maintain moderate loads (3×6–8 for main lifts).
- Wed — Tempo: Warm‑up. 15–18 min continuous tempo (or 3×6 min). Cool‑down.

- Take SABA 10–15 minutes before the session if that is his usual GP-prescribed routine. Carry inhaler during sessions.
- Prefer shorter, controlled hard efforts rather than long all-out sprints early on. Keep intensity controlled (target RPE and pace guidance below).
- On very cold days or poor air quality, move intervals indoors or postpone.
- If coughing/wheeze/chest tightness occurs during intervals: stop, use inhaler, rest. If symptoms do not resolve or inhaler use increases compared to baseline, consult GP.
- Limit interval sessions to 1–2 per week at peak — start with one per week and add a second only if fully tolerated.

Interval session format and intensity cues
- Structure: Warm-up (15 min) → Main set (intervals) → Cool-down (8–10 min).
- Intensity targets:
  - Short repeats (20–60 s): ~85–95% of max running speed; RPE 7–8/10 (short bursts).
  - Medium repeats (90 s – 3 min): at or slightly faster than target 5K pace; RPE 7–8/10 (controlled hard).
  - Long repeats (>3 min up to 5 min): at near 5K pace to slightly slower; RPE 7/10 (sustainable for set).
- Recovery: Active recovery (easy jog or brisk walk). Start with equal or slightly longer recovery than work (e.g., 1:1 to 1:2 work:rest by time). Shorter recoveries can be used later as tolerance improves.
- Progression principle: Increase total hard time or intensity by ~10% per week maximum, or decrease recovery slightly. If asthma symptoms increase, revert or reduce intensity.

Week-by-week interval sessions (these replace or specify one interval session per week; in later weeks a second interval session is added)
Weeks 1–4 — introduction to short pickups/strides (NOT full intervals)
- Week 1–2: Strides only
  - After warm-up: 4×20–25 s strides at ~80–85% effort, full recovery (90–120 s walking) between.
  - Purpose: turnover, neuromuscular prep, minimal airway provocation.
- Week 3: Slightly longer pickups
  - After warm-up: 6×30 s pickups at ~85% effort with 90–120 s easy jog/walk recovery.
- Week 4: Progress to 6×40 s pickups with 90–120 s recovery.
  - If any wheeze or cough occurs, keep to shorter pickups and/or reduce to 4–5 reps.

Weeks 5–6 — short interval sets (building tolerance)
- Week 5 (Intro interval session)
  - Warm-up (15 min).
  - Main set: 6×1 min at a brisk controlled pace (around a comfortable pace faster than steady runs but not all-out). Recovery 2 min easy jog/walk.
  - Total hard time = 6 min. Cool-down 8–10 min.
  - RPE target for work: ~7/10.
- Week 6
  - Warm-up.
  - Main set: 8×1 min at similar intensity with 90–120 s recovery.
  - OR alternative: 5×90 s at slightly faster pace with 2 min recovery.
  - Cool-down.

Weeks 7–8 — medium-length intervals and shorter recoveries
- Week 7
  - Warm-up.
  - Main set: 6×90 s at near target 5K pace (RPE 7–8/10). Recovery: 90 s easy jog.
  - Cool-down.
- Week 8
  - Warm-up.
  - Main set: 4×2 min at 5K pace with 2–2.5 min jog recovery.
  - Option B (if tolerated): 10×1 min at slightly faster than 5K pace with 60–90 s recovery.

Weeks 9–10 — increase intensity and specificity (add a second interval session if tolerated)
- Week 9 (one interval session focusing on quality)
  - Warm-up.
  - Main set: 5×3 min at slightly slower than 5K pace (or at threshold pace) with 2–3 min recovery jog.
  - Purpose: raise lactate threshold and hold faster pace longer.
  - Cool-down.
- Week 10 (two interval sessions optional; pick one harder, one shorter)
  - Harder session (mid-week):
    - Warm-up.
    - Main set: 6×800 m or 6×2 min at 5K pace with 90–120 s jog recovery. Aim for consistent effort.
    - Cool-down.
  - Shorter speed session (earlier week or later):
    - Warm-up.
    - Main set: 8×90 s at slightly faster than 5K pace with 60–90 s recovery. Cool-down.
  - Note: add the second session only if the client tolerated previous weeks well and asthma symptoms remain controlled.

Weeks 11–12 — sharpening, race-specific intervals, then taper
- Week 11 (peak intensity week — proceed cautiously)
  - Session A (intervals—quality):
    - Warm-up.
    - Main set option 1: 5×1 km at goal 5K pace with 90–120 s recovery jog.
    - Option 2 (if 1 km repeats are too provoking): 8×600 m at goal pace with 90 s recovery.
    - Aim: practice goal race pace with precise effort.
    - Cool-down.
  - Session B (secondary tempo/interval mix):
    - Warm-up.
    - Main set: 3×5 min at tempo/comfortably hard pace with 2–3 min recovery (builds sustained pace tolerance).
    - Cool-down.
  - Strength sessions: reduce load/volume mid-week to preserve legs.

- Week 12 (taper and sharpen)
  - Early-week short sharpening session (48–72 hours before race/test):
    - Warm-up (thorough).
    - Main set: 6–8×30–45 s pick-ups a little faster than 5K pace with full recovery (90–120 s). Alternatively 4×60 s at near 5K pace with 2 min recovery.
    - Keep total hard time low (under ~6–8 minutes).
    - Cool-down.
  - Race day (or 5K test): Warm up 15+ min including 4–6 strides, run 5K at target pace.
  - Post-race: long cool-down walk/jog and recovery.

How to progress/recover between intervals
- If the client reports increased inhaler use, cough, or prolonged wheeze after interval sessions, drop intensity: shorter repeats (30–60 s) and longer recoveries, or revert to base runs for 7–14 days.
- Always include an easy recovery day after a hard interval session (easy walk/run or rest).
- Keep strength work lighter in the 48–72 hours before interval sessions — especially the heavy lower-body lifts. Place heavier strength session 48+ hours away from the hardest interval day.

Sample detailed interval session examples (copy to hand him)
- Beginner interval (Week 5)
  - Warm-up 15 min incl. 4 strides.
  - 6×1:00 brisk run (RPE 7/10) with 2:00 easy jog/walk recovery.
  - Cool-down 8–10 min.
- Medium interval (Week 8)
  - Warm-up 15 min incl. 4–6 strides.
  - 4×2:00 at 5K pace (RPE 7–8/10) with 2:00–2:30 jog recovery.
  - Cool-down 8–10 min.
- Race-pace interval (Week 11)
  - Warm-up 15 min incl. 6 strides.
  - 5×1000 m at target 5K pace with 1:30–2:00 easy jog recovery.
  - Cool-down 10 min.
- Sharpening (Week 12)
  - Warm-up 15 min incl. 4–6 strides.
  - 6×30–45 s pickups a bit faster than 5K pace, full recoveries 90–120 s.
  - Cool-down.

Asthma-specific interval tips
- Keep early intervals short and controlled; medium repeats can be introduced only if symptoms are well controlled.
- Encourage diaphragmatic/nasal breathing during easy recovery sections; exhale during exertion to prevent throat dryness.
- If cold: wear a buff, extend warm-up, and consider doing intervals on treadmill to control environment.
- Track post-session symptoms (wheeze, cough, extra inhaler use) on a simple log to decide whether to progress.

Monitoring and decision rules for the trainer
- Use a simple traffic-light rule after every interval session:
  - Green: no extra inhaler use, minimal cough/wheeze, recovered in 10–15 min → progress as planned.
  - Amber: required SABA once or brief cough/wheeze resolved within 10–20 min → hold progression for 1 week, reduce hard time by ~25%.
  - Red: persistent wheeze or required more than normal inhaler usage, symptoms lasting >20 min → pause intervals, revert to base plan and advise medical review.
- Record RPE for each interval and general recovery RPE to monitor overtraining or airway issues.

Where tempo fits in the weekly structure

- Strength timing: avoid very heavy lower‑body strength within 48 hours before tempo or interval sessions; schedule heavy strength 72+ hours from hard run if possible.

Tempo run definitions and intensity
- Tempo run = sustained “comfortably hard” effort that is faster than easy runs but sustainable for 20–30 minutes total (tempo portion). RPE ~6–7/10.
- Pace guidance: roughly “comfortably hard” — conversational ability: short sentences only. If you have no pace data, use RPE rather than exact times.
- For asthma: extend warm‑up (15 min) and include progressive accelerations and 4 strides; consider SABA 10–15 min prior if that’s his routine.

Week 7 — Intro to tempo
- Tempo session (Wed):
  - Warm‑up 12–15 min (include strides).
  - Main: 2×6 min tempo at comfortably hard pace with 3 min easy jog between sets.
  - Total tempo time = 12 min.
  - Cool‑down 8–10 min.
- Purpose: introduce sustained effort without long continuous stress.

Week 8 — Increase tempo time
- Tempo session:
  - Warm‑up.
  - Main: 1×12–15 min continuous tempo (aim for 12–15 min at tempo pace) OR 2×8 min with 2–3 min recovery.
  - Cool‑down.

Week 9 — Build intensity/duration
- Tempo session:
  - Warm‑up.
  - Main: 15–18 min continuous tempo OR 3×6 min with 2 min jog between (total 18 min).
  - Cool‑down.

Week 10 — Race‑specific tempo
- Tempo session:
  - Warm‑up.
  - Main: 20 min continuous tempo at a steady comfortably hard pace (RPE ~6–7/10). If this is too much, do 3×7 min with 2 min recoveries.
  - Cool‑down.

Week 11 — High quality tempo
- Tempo session:
  - Warm‑up.
  - Main: 2×10–12 min at tempo pace with 3 min easy jog between (total 20–24 min tempo).
  - Cool‑down.
- Keep strength lighter mid‑week if intervals also performed this week.

Week 12 — Taper and sharpen (reduce volume)
- Tempo session (early in week, not within 48–72 hours of race/test):
  - Warm‑up.
  - Main: 10–12 min tempo OR 3×5 min at tempo pace with 2 min recovery — keep intensity but lower volume.
  - Cool‑down.
- Keep the last hard workout (short pickups/strides) 48–72 hours before the 5K test.

How to combine tempo with intervals and strength
- Interval day remains the primary speed stimulus (shorter, higher intensity). Tempo is the sustained threshold stimulus.
- Schedule: place tempo mid‑week (Wed) and interval on Fri or vice versa, with an easy run or rest between.
- Strength: place heavier strength session 48+ hours away from tempo. Lighter maintenance strength can go 24 hours after tempo if client tolerates it.
- Example mid‑season week (Week 10):
  - Mon: Easy run
  - Tue: Strength 1 (heavier)
  - Wed: Tempo 20 min (main)
  - Thu: Strength 2 (lighter)
  - Fri: Interval session (shorter or moderate)
  - Sat: Easy long run or rest
  - Sun: Rest

Asthma and tempo specifics
- Extended warm‑up before tempo days is mandatory; include breathing drills and lung‑opening mobility.
- Keep tempo intensity conservative — target sustainable effort rather than chasing exact paces early on.
- If wheeze/cough increases after tempo sessions, reduce tempo duration by ~25% and increase recovery between repeats; consult GP if symptoms persist.

  - Warm‑up 15 min.

Monitoring and progression rules

- Increase tempo duration no more than ~10–20% per week.
- Keep only one true hard interval session per week when tempo sessions are in place; if adding a second interval, reduce volume.

Below I’ll show how to slot a Parkrun into Week 8 safely for a client with exercise‑induced asthma, including the lead‑in week adjustments, the exact week‑8 schedule (runs, strength, warm‑ups), race‑day warm‑up and inhaler guidance, pacing strategy, and recovery plan after the Parkrun.

Summary recommendation
- Do Parkrun on the scheduled Week 8 long/run day (commonly Saturday morning).
- Treat Parkrun as a test: aim for a controlled, realistic effort rather than an all‑out race. Use it to assess pacing, symptom response to continuous 5K, and readiness for later speed work.
- Prioritize an extended warm‑up and asthma precautions (SABA use 10–15 min before if that’s his routine; carry inhaler; use buff in cold weather).
- Reduce training load in the 48–72 hours before Parkrun to arrive fresh.

Lead‑in adjustments (Week 7 → Week 8)
- In the week prior (Week 7), avoid very heavy strength or maximal interval sessions 48–72 hours before Parkrun (i.e., no heavy lower‑body lifts on Thu/ Fri; move them earlier in the week).
- Keep interval work earlier in Week 7 light to moderate (short repeats) so Week 8 Parkrun is a realistic test.
- In Week 8, reduce total training volume/day before Parkrun: keep Thursday strength light and Friday an easy 20–25 min jog with 4–6 short strides in the warm‑up (do NOT do hard intervals the day before).

Suggested Week 8 schedule (example Monday–Sunday)
- Mon: Easy recovery run 20–30 min (easy pace). Strength Session 1 (moderate) can be moved to Tue if preferred.
- Tue: Strength 1 (moderate) — lower volume than usual if he feels tired.
- Wed: Tempo run (shorter than usual): 10–12 min tempo or 2×6 min tempo with 3 min recovery. Keep intensity controlled.
- Thu: Strength 2 (light) — mobility and activation only.
- Fri: Easy 20–25 min jog + warm‑up strides (4×20–25 s) — keep it relaxed.
- Sat: Parkrun (5K) — race/test day. See race‑day plan below.
- Sun: Recovery — walking, gentle cycling, or complete rest.

Pre‑Parkrun (race‑day) checklist and warm‑up
- SABA inhaler: take 10–15 minutes before warm‑up if that is his prescribed routine; have it on hand during the run.
- Clothing: in cold weather use a buff/scarf and layer; warm drinks before the race can help. In hot weather dress lightly and hydrate.
- Nutrition: small carbohydrate snack 60–90 min before (banana, toast); avoid heavy meals.
- Hydration: normal. Parkrun courses are short; mid‑run hydration not required.
- Warm‑up (15–20 min total; extended because of EIA):
  1. 5–8 min brisk walk → easy jog (gradually increase breathing).
  2. Dynamic drills: leg swings, hip circles, walking lunges (2–3 min).
  3. 4–6 progressive strides: 20–30 s accelerations, not sprints; full recovery walk/jog between.
  4. Final 2 min easy jog, a couple of deep diaphragmatic breaths.
- If cold: extend the walking portion to keep airways warm; do strides wearing a buff.

Pacing strategy for Parkrun (goal: test, not all‑out)
- Target effort: controlled 5K effort — RPE 7/10 if testing fitness; if this is his first continuous 5K aim for RPE 6–7/10 to prioritize symptom control.
- Suggested pacing options:
  - Conservative test (recommended if first 5K): even pace or slight negative split — start at comfortable pace for first 1 km (RPE 6), settle into slightly harder pace for km 2–3 (RPE 7), only push final km if breathing and legs feel good.
  - Slightly ambitious test (if comfortable with 25–30 min continuous runs previously): aim for even 5K race pace with controlled second half push. Monitor breathing; back off if wheeze/cough appears.
- Use walking breaks only if needed for asthma symptoms — it's better to slow to easy jog/walk briefly than push through severe wheeze.

Asthma-specific race guidance
- Avoid going hard immediately on the first 100–200 m — rapid early surge can trigger EIA.
- If he experiences cough/wheeze during Parkrun, stop, use inhaler, and take a walk break until symptoms settle. Encourage him not to chase time if symptoms worsen.
- Monitor inhaler usage: record if he needed it pre-race and post-race. If he requires additional puffs more than usual, note this and consider medical review.

Post‑Parkrun recovery (first 48 hours)
- Immediate cool‑down: 8–12 min easy walking/jogging and breathing control, then light stretching.
- Post‑run nutrition: carbohydrate + protein within 60 min (yogurt + fruit, smoothie).
- Recovery day(s): Sunday easy active recovery or rest. Avoid heavy strength lifts for 48 hours post‑Parkrun if legs are sore.
- Monitor for delayed asthma symptoms (wheezing, cough that persists). If symptoms persist or inhaler use increases for days after, advise GP review.

How to use Parkrun feedback to adjust training
- If successful with minimal symptoms: use result to inform target pace in later interval and tempo sessions. For example, if he runs 27:00, pace per km ~5:24 — use this to plan 5K pace repeats.
- If he completed Parkrun but with mild symptoms that resolved quickly: consider slowing pace or increasing warm‑up for future hard sessions; continue base building and resume intervals with slightly reduced intensity for 1 week.
- If he needed inhaler more than usual or had prolonged symptoms: take 7–14 days of reduced intensity (easy runs only) and consult GP about controller therapy and airway management before resuming intervals/tempos.

Example Parkrun day plan (step‑by‑step)
- 60–90 min pre‑run: light snack (banana), hydrate.
- 15 min pre‑warm‑up: take SABA inhaler (if per GP routine).
- Warm‑up (15–20 min): 5–8 min walk/jog, mobility, 4–6 strides.
- 5K Parkrun: start conservatively, stick to pacing plan, carry inhaler.
- Cool‑down: 8–12 min easy walking/jogging; gentle static stretches.
- Post‑run: small recovery snack; rest that afternoon; easy recovery on Sunday.

Notes for the trainer
- Position this Parkrun as a learning/test — encourage him to treat it as data gathering for pacing and symptom response rather than a must‑hit PR.
- Bring spare inhaler or ensure he always has it.
- If you're present, help keep his start conservative (avoid aggressive starts with crowds).
- Record finishing time, perceived exertion, and any inhaler use or symptoms to guide week 9–12 pacing and interval intensity.

- Running shoes (broken‑in, not brand new), socks.

- SABA inhaler on person (plus spare if available).

If things go well — post‑test progression
- If the test is completed comfortably with minimal asthma symptoms, continue planned Week 13 progression (if you want to extend training) with adjusted interval and tempo targets based on Parkrun time.

- Strength 1 (Tue): 30–35 min — posterior chain, single‑leg strength, core. 3 sets of main lifts, 60–90 s rest.
- Strength 2 (Thu): 20–25 min — maintenance circuit, mobility, breathing drills. 2 rounds.
- Avoid heavy lower‑body lifts within 48–72 hours of the heaviest interval session; in Week 12 keep strength very light.

Progression notes for intervals & tempo
- Intervals introduced Week 5 and progress in duration and specificity through Weeks 11–12.
- Tempo runs start Week 7 and build to 20 min tempo by Week 10.
- Limit hard interval sessions to 1 per week until Week 9; add a second short session in Week 10 only if tolerated.
- Use RPE and symptom log to guide progression. Traffic‑light rule: Green (no extra inhaler, OK) → progress; Amber (extra single inhaler puff, brief symptoms) → hold/step back; Red (prolonged symptoms/more inhaler) → revert to base & GP review.

Full 12‑Week program (week-by-week). Each week lists 3 run sessions and 2 strength sessions. Warm‑up/cool‑down and asthma precautions apply to all sessions.

Weeks 1–2 — Establish routine, breathing control, long warm‑ups
Goal: get moving regularly, practice long warm‑ups and breathing, introduce light strength.

Week 1
- Mon — Run A (20–25 min): Warm‑up 12–15 min. 6×(1:00 easy jog + 2:00 brisk walk). Cool‑down.
- Tue — Strength 1 (30 min): Glute bridge 3×12; Bodyweight squat 3×12; Reverse lunges 3×8/leg; Plank 3×30 s; Single‑leg calf raise 3×12/leg.
- Wed — Run B (20 min): Warm‑up. 8×(1:00 jog + 1:30 walk). Cool‑down.
- Thu — Strength 2 (20 min): 2 rounds circuit: Step‑ups 12/leg; Side‑lying clamshell 12/side; Band row 12/arm; Dead bug 10/side.
- Fri — Run C (21 min): Warm‑up. 6×(1:30 jog + 2:00 walk). Cool‑down.
- Sat — Optional easy walk/mobility.
- Sun — Rest.

Week 2
- Mon — Run A: 1:00 jog + 2:00 walk ×6 (same as Wk1 A).
- Tue — Strength 1: same as Week 1; focus on form.
- Wed — Run B: 1:00 jog +1:30 walk ×8 (same).
- Thu — Strength 2: same circuit, 2 rounds.
- Fri — Run C: 1:30 jog + 2:00 walk ×6.
- Sat/Sun — Recovery/rest.

Weeks 3–4 — Increase interval lengths; begin light loaded strength
Goal: longer continuous intervals, introduce goblet/DB exercises.

Week 3
- Mon — Run A: Warm‑up. 7×(2:00 jog + 2:00 walk). Cool‑down.
- Tue — Strength 1: Single‑leg glute bridge 3×10/leg; Goblet squat 3×10; Bulgarian split squat 3×8/leg; Side plank 3×25–30 s; RDL (light DB) 3×8–10; Calf raises 3×15.
- Wed — Run B: Warm‑up. 6×(3:00 jog + 2:00 walk). Cool‑down.
- Thu — Strength 2: Circuit 2 rounds: Single‑leg RDL 10/leg; Push‑ups 10–12; Pallof press 10–12/side; Walking lunges 10/leg.
- Fri — Run C: Warm‑up. 3×(5:00 jog + 3:00 walk). Cool‑down.
- Sat/Sun — Recovery.

Week 4
- Mon — Run A: Warm‑up. 6×(4:00 jog + 2:00 walk) OR 7×(3:00 + 2:00) if preferred.
- Tue — Strength 1: Progress weight slightly on goblet/DB RDLs; 3 sets each.
- Wed — Run B: Warm‑up. 5×(5:00 jog + 3:00 walk).
- Thu — Strength 2: 2–3 rounds circuit (as Week 3).
- Fri — Run C: Warm‑up. 2×(8:00 jog + 3:00 walk) or 3×(5:00 +3:00).
- Sat/Sun — Active recovery/rest.

Weeks 5–6 — Move toward continuous running; introduce intervals
Goal: longer continuous blocks, first interval session introduced, increase strength load.

Week 5
- Mon — Run A: Warm‑up. 2×(8:00 easy jog + 3:00 walk). Cool‑down.
- Tue — Strength 1: DB RDL 3×8; Bulgarian split squat 3×8–10/leg; Step‑ups (weighted) 3×10/leg; Single‑leg glute bridge 3×10/leg; Plank w/arm reach 3×30–40 s; Calf raises 3×12–15.
- Wed — Run B (Interval intro): Warm‑up 15 min incl. 4 strides. 6×1:00 brisk runs (RPE ~7/10) with 2:00 easy jog/walk recovery. Cool‑down 8–10 min.
- Thu — Strength 2: 2–3 rounds: Kettlebell swings 12–15; TRX row 12; Lateral lunges 10/side; Bird‑dog 10/side.
- Fri — Run C: Warm‑up. Continuous 15 min easy jog + 5 min walk + 10 min easy jog (or 2×12 min with short walk). Cool‑down.
- Sat/Sun — Easy activity/rest.

Week 6
- Mon — Run A: Warm‑up. 20 min continuous easy run (if tolerated) or 2×10 min with 2 min walk.
- Tue — Strength 1: increase load on RDLs/step‑ups modestly.
- Wed — Run B (Intervals): Warm‑up 15 min. 8×1:00 brisk with 90–120 s recovery OR 5×90 s at slightly faster pace with 2:00 recovery. Cool‑down.
- Thu — Strength 2: lighter maintenance circuit + breathing drills.
- Fri — Run C: Warm‑up. 2×10–12 min easy jog with 2–3 min recovery between. Cool‑down.
- Sat/Sun — Rest/active recovery.

Weeks 7–8 — Build continuous time, introduce tempo, and Parkrun test in Week 8
Goal: 20–30 min continuous run capability; tempo introduction Week 7; Parkrun Week 8 (controlled test).

Week 7
- Mon — Run A: Warm‑up. 20 min continuous easy run. Cool‑down.
- Tue — Strength 1: heavier session — trap‑bar/DB RDL 3×5–8; Bulgarian split squat 3×8; Farmer carry 3×40–60 m; Hanging knee raise 3×10–12; calf work.
- Wed — Tempo (Intro): Warm‑up (15 min). 2×6 min tempo (RPE 6–7/10) with 3:00 easy jog between. Cool‑down.
- Thu — Strength 2: 2 rounds lighter circuit + mobility.
- Fri — Run C (Fartlek/light): Warm‑up. 20–25 min easy run with 6×30–45 s pickups (85% effort) with full recovery. Cool‑down.
- Sat — Easy walk or rest.
- Sun — Rest.

Week 8 — Parkrun test week (Parkrun on Sat)
- Monday — Run A: Easy 20–30 min. Strength 1 (move to Tue if preferred).
- Tuesday — Strength 1: moderate, reduce volume if feeling tired.
- Wednesday — Tempo: 10–12 min tempo OR 2×6 min tempo (shorter than usual) — keep intensity controlled.
- Thursday — Strength 2: light mobility and activation only.
- Friday — Easy 20–25 min + 4 strides in warm‑up; keep relaxed.
- Saturday — Parkrun (5K test). Race day plan:
  - 60–90 min pre: small carb snack; SABA 10–15 min before warm‑up if that’s his routine.
  - Warm‑up 15–20 min: walk → easy jog → mobility → 4–6 strides.
  - Race: conservative start; even/small negative split strategy. Carry inhaler.
  - Cool‑down 8–12 min + recovery snack.
- Sunday — Recovery: rest or easy active recovery. Monitor asthma; avoid heavy strength for 48 hours after Parkrun.

Weeks 9–10 — Build intensity and intervals; tempo to 20 min
Goal: consolidate endurance, add structured interval and tempo stimulus. May add second interval session in Week 10 if tolerated.

Week 9
- Mon — Run A: 25–30 min continuous easy run (conversational).
- Tue — Strength 1: maintain moderate loads (3×6–8 for main lifts).
- Wed — Tempo: Warm‑up. 15–18 min continuous tempo (or 3×6 min). Cool‑down.
- Thu — Strength 2: maintenance circuit & breathing practice.
- Fri — Intervals: Warm‑up 15 min. 5×3:00 at slightly slower than 5K pace (threshold) with 2–3 min jog recovery. Cool‑down.
- Sat — Easy 25–30 min or rest.
- Sun — Rest.

Week 10
- Mon — Run A: 30–35 min easy/steady with middle 10 min slightly brisk.
- Tue — Strength 1: moderate session; reduce heavy lifting if intervals coming later.
- Wed — Tempo: 20 min continuous tempo (RPE 6–7/10). Cool‑down.
- Thu — Strength 2: light circuit.
- Fri — Intervals (harder): Warm‑up. 6×800 m or 6×2:00 at 5K pace with 90–120 s recovery. Cool‑down.
- Sat — Easy recovery run/walk.
- Sun — Rest.

Weeks 11–12 — Peak intensity then taper; sharpening; race prep Week 12
Goal: Week 11 peak interval quality; Week 12 taper, sharpen, and race (or final test).

Week 11 (peak)
- Mon — Run A: 30 min easy run.
- Tue — Strength 1: moderate but reduce volume to preserve freshness for intervals.
- Wed — Tempo / Mixed: 2×10–12 min tempo with 3:00 recovery (total 20–24 min tempo) OR 25 min tempo if well tolerated.
- Thu — Strength 2: light mobility session; no heavy loading.
- Fri — Intervals (quality): Warm‑up 15 min. Main set options (pick one according to tolerance):
  - Option 1: 5×1 km at goal 5K pace with 90–120 s recovery.
  - Option 2: 8×600 m at goal pace with 90 s recovery.
  Monitor symptoms; do not force full RPE 9+ efforts if asthma flares.
- Sat — Easy 25–30 min or rest.
- Sun — Rest.

Week 12 — Finisher / Race‑day prep week (taper)
(Assume race/test on Saturday; adjust if different)
- Monday — Easy 20–25 min + light Strength 1 activation (very light): 2×12 glute bridges etc.
- Tuesday — Sharpening intervals (short): Warm‑up. 6×1:00 slightly faster than race pace with 90–120 s recovery (quality, not maximal). Cool‑down.
- Wednesday — Easy 20 min + breathing drills; stride 2×20 s optional.
- Thursday — Rest or very light jog/walk + mobility.
- Friday — Pre‑race tune: Warm‑up 10–12 min + 3–4×30 s strides; keep legs loose; final equipment check; SABA only if prescribed/required before warm‑up on race day.
- Saturday — Race/Test day (5K). Full race warm‑up 15–20 min incl. strides; conservative start; even or negative split pacing. Carry inhaler and use if needed. Cool‑down 8–12 min and recovery snack.
- Sunday — Recovery: rest/light activity; monitor asthma for delayed symptoms. Avoid heavy strength for 48–72 hours.

Post‑race follow‑up guidance
- If race completed with minimal symptoms: use finishing time to set 5K pace for future tempo/interval targets. Continue training with adjusted intensity or plan next training block.
- If increased inhaler use or prolonged symptoms: take 7–14 days reduced intensity, no intervals/tempos; consult GP about possible controller therapy before returning to heavy training.

Nutrition & recovery summary
- Pre‑session: small carb snack 30–90 min before (banana, toast). Avoid heavy meals.
- Post‑session: protein + carb within 60 min (yogurt + fruit, smoothie).
- Hydration: steady daily hydration; sip during longer sessions >40 min.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours/night.
- Cold weather: warm pre‑session drink, buff; extend warm‑up to keep airways warm.

Monitoring & logs
- Keep a session log: distance/time, RPE, inhaler use (pre, during, post), any cough/wheeze, recovery notes.
- Use the traffic‑light rule after hard sessions:
  - Green: no extra inhaler use, minimal symptoms → continue progression.
  - Amber: needed an extra puff or brief symptoms → hold progression for a week and reduce hard volume.
  - Red: persistent or increased symptoms → stop intervals, revert to base, seek GP review.
